opening.welcome: You're going to paint a misty autumn birch grove, with a leaf-covered path running back into the fog. The heart of it is the pair of big leaning birches against the gold haze, with the path opening next to them. What makes it sing is the contrast: warm gold leaves and white bark in front of cool blue fog.
opening.light: The low sun shines through the trees from behind, so the near side of the wood glows gold while the pines and the far side sit in cool blue shade. The birch trunks and the leaves catch that sun on the side facing it.

skills.how: Dabbing is tapping with the tip of a nearly dry brush, so each tap leaves a leaf. It builds the golden bushes, the leaves overhead and the carpet of fallen leaves, always dark first, then gold, then the sunlit ones. Watch for blobs: they mean a wet or overloaded brush, so wipe it on a towel.

Dry brush is a brush with almost no paint and no water, skimmed lightly so the paint catches only the canvas texture. It makes the mist, the shadow on the path, and the shade and light on the birch bark. If it goes on solid, the brush held too much paint.

Thick to thin is pressing the full width of the brush, then turning onto its edge and easing off so the mark tapers. It pulls the far misty trunks, the big birch trunks and the dark bark marks. Press firmly where the mark should be wide, and lift gently where it should end.

opening.road: First comes the misty background: the blue glow, a far trunk and a veil of mist, so the depth is there before anything solid goes on. Next the near woods: the dark pines and the golden bushes, each built dark to light. Then the ground and its path, with a shadow and the mossy rock. The birches come after that, over everything behind them, because they are the subject. Last come the gold leaves overhead, the fallen leaves, and the brightest sunlit leaves that finish it.

the-background.for: This stage lays the foggy blue wood that everything else stands in.
the-background.end: The whole canvas is a soft blue fog with faint pale trunks, darker tree shapes and a faint warm glow.

the-near-woods.for: This stage builds the dark pines and the golden bushes that make the near woods.
the-near-woods.end: Dark blue-green pines with soft gray-green light stand in the fog, and a big glowing gold bush mass faces them across a gap where the path will run, with fog still filling the ground.

the-ground.for: This stage lays the leafy ground with its pale path, a shadow, and the mossy rock.
the-ground.end: Warm orange ground with a pale path runs back between the bushes and the pines, and a round mossy rock sits at the foot of the pines.

the-birches.for: This stage paints the birches, the subject, over everything behind them.
the-birches.end: White birch trunks with gray shade and dark broken bark marks stand in front of the woods, darkest at their feet.

the-canopy.for: This stage hangs the gold leaves overhead, over the trunk tops.
the-canopy.end: Clusters of gold leaves hang across the sky in front of the trunks, with darker leaves peeking out and fog showing between them.

the-fallen-leaves.for: This stage covers the ground in fallen leaves, dark ones first.
the-fallen-leaves.end: The ground is a carpet of orange, gold, red-brown and gray leaves, big in front and small toward the path's far end.

the-last-lights.for: This stage adds the brightest sunlit leaves that finish the painting.
the-last-lights.end: The finished painting: pale sunlit leaves glow overhead, on the bushes and along the path, against the blue fog.
